A.title: Everyday travel
A.body: First, please tell us about the transport options you currently use and the types of journeys you make. These questions are about your actual circumstances; there are no right or wrong answers.

purposes.title: The different journeys you make
purposes.body: The same person may use different transport modes for commuting, errands and leisure. The next two questions ask about these purposes separately. There is no assumption that everyone works, studies or makes weekly leisure journeys.

journey.title: One real journey
journey.body: Think about one real one-way journey you have made regularly during the past four weeks, for example for work or study, errands or care, or leisure. Please use this same journey for the ordinary-travel questions. We will return to it after the separate hypothetical 2030 trip. If you have no recurring journey, you can say so.

B.title: A future trip in 2030
B.body: The next questions concern a hypothetical 20 km one-way weekday trip in 2030. This trip is separate from the ordinary journey you just described.

scenario.title: Imagine the same 20 km trip
scenario.body:
Imagine one adult making the same 20 km one-way weekday trip in 2030. Each option shows the total amount your household would pay for that trip, total door-to-door time, the chance of arriving within five minutes of the planned time, and walking/wheeling time. Walking/wheeling and waiting are already included in total time. Costs are stated in current-purchasing-power euros.

Consider driving only if you could legally drive, or travelling as a passenger only if an authorised household driver is available. A private or shared EV here is a household arrangement, not a promised autonomous taxi. Consider public transport only where an accessible service is feasible. If no displayed offer suits you, choose “None of these.”

C.title: Return to your ordinary journey
C.body: Now return to the ordinary journey you described earlier. The next statements ask about one transport option you might use more often, or continue using, for that ordinary journey—not about the hypothetical 2030 trip.

D.title: Vehicles, parking and charging
D.body: The next questions are about your current circumstances. You do not need to own a vehicle or charge one yourself. Questions about actual plug-in vehicle charging will appear only when they are relevant to your household and you can describe the arrangements.

S.title: About this questionnaire test
S.body: This version tests the flow and clarity of questions about everyday travel, parked wireless charging and vehicle-to-grid services. You may use your circumstances or fictional answers. Please do not enter names or contact details. If you choose Submit at the end, your test answers, route and active time are saved for improving the questionnaire. Screen comments stay in this browser tab and can be downloaded separately. You may leave before submitting. This is not the main research survey and does not activate any service.

E.title: Two possible charging and energy services
E.body: These are hypothetical services for testing the questions. A suitable compatible vehicle and equipment are assumed only where the scenario says so. Wireless charging, vehicle-to-grid export and automated positioning are separate capabilities.

wpt.title: Stationary wireless charging
wpt.body: Stationary wireless charging transfers electricity to a compatible EV while it is parked above compatible equipment. The driver or an authorised positioning system must place the vehicle correctly. It is not charging while driving. Charging speed, compatibility and reliability depend on the installation and operating conditions.

v2g.title: Vehicle-to-grid or V2G
v2g.body: V2G lets a compatible EV battery send electricity to the grid through suitable bidirectional equipment. It may help balance electricity demand and supply, depending on how the service operates. Participation depends on an agreement about battery reserve, ready time, control, data and payment. Payments or environmental benefits are not guaranteed. V2G is different from V2H, which supplies a home rather than the grid.

positioning.title: Automated positioning
positioning.body: Automated positioning moves a compatible vehicle into a specified parked position under authorised supervision and stop controls. It is separate from charging and does not authorise electricity export or imply driverless road travel.

F.title: Consider the service for your own role
F.body: Imagine a suitable compatible vehicle and the described service were available to you or your household. Answer for your own role in using it or taking part in decisions. The operator means the organisation running the service and dealing with users’ requests. No particular organisation is named. Choose Cannot judge if you need more information.

wpt_gate.title: A planned parking stop
wpt_gate.body: Imagine a place where you would already park for two hours, such as work, shops or another destination. You are comparing charging during that stay, rather than an urgent fast-charging stop.

wpt_terms.title: The same parking stay and energy
wpt_terms.body:
In this hypothetical comparison, compatible equipment is provided, there is no queue and setup takes two minutes. Both cable and wireless options deliver 20 kWh to the battery during the same two-hour stay. The displayed total price includes conversion losses. Extra round-trip driving is a detour outside the two hours. €10 for 20 kWh means €0.50 per delivered kWh.

No-restart sessions means completion without interrupting the session to restart it, out of 100 attempts. If wireless needs a restart, cable fallback is available at the same location, with connection assistance if needed. For this test scenario its €10 total replaces the wireless charge; there is no double charge, and 20 kWh is still delivered before departure.

Driver with guidance means an authorised driver positions the vehicle. Automatic positioning uses an authorised system with supervision and a stop control. Neither means driverless road travel. Renewable share is the annual purchased-supply allocation, not the electricity mix at that moment. These are proposed test terms, not a service guarantee.

v2g_terms.title: A hypothetical V2G arrangement
v2g_terms.body:
Imagine a compatible 60 kWh EV and suitable charging point. Compare offers over 12 months. Equipment, installation and joining have no additional household charge. No V2G means ordinary one-way smart charging, no grid export and no availability payment.

On the agreed one, three or five weekdays each week, the vehicle is connected for a six-hour overnight window. At most one export event occurs on an active weekday, lasting at most two hours and exporting at most 6 kWh. Arrival charge varies. Export stops at the protected reserve; if arrival charge is below that reserve, no export is permitted until charging raises it above the reserve. The reserve is a floor for export, not a promise of current charge or driving range.

You can stop export or unplug immediately. Restoration to 80% charge for a declared departure needs at least four hours’ notice. An unexpected departure does not promise immediate restoration. Each-event approval, automatic notice and automatic with a dashboard record differ; all retain a stop control and withdrawal.

v2g_payment.title: The provider pays your household
v2g_payment.body:
Payment is for the agreed availability hours, up to the monthly maximum shown. Connected hours with the agreed permissions count even if the provider requests no export; the agreed reserve does not by itself reduce payment. Disconnected hours or hours affected by declining/overriding a requested event do not count. There is no extra fine or exit fee.

Example: at a €60 monthly maximum, meeting half the agreed hours pays €30 to your household. Exported electricity, restoration electricity and extra conversion losses are reimbursed separately. Ordinary travel-energy costs remain yours and are equal across offers.

The hypothetical contract covers independently verified additional battery damage attributable to V2G, excluding normal ageing. It uses battery status, declared departure and energy-flow information, without route tracking. Renewable share is an annual purchased-supply allocation, not guaranteed instantaneous renewable power or emissions savings. These proposed terms need partner testing; they do not promise earnings or home backup power.

public.title: Now consider people in the local area
public.body: Think about making [TECH] available in [SITE], including people who might never use it. Some households would have compatible vehicles or equipment and others would not. The operator would run the service, but local locations and who funds installation are not settled in this description. No service is being approved by this survey. Choose Cannot judge if these missing facts prevent a judgement.

benefits.title: Possible benefits and your priorities
benefits.body: These are possible benefits, not promises. A benefit can be unimportant or irrelevant to you. Please give your own view rather than what you think the project wants to hear.

values.title: Guiding principles in your life
values.body: How important is each value as a guiding principle in your life? Use 1 Not important at all to 7 Extremely important. Please try not to give more than two values a seven; you can still continue or prefer not to answer. This is a test of the adapted values format.

H.title: A few final background questions
H.body: These help us check how the questions work for different circumstances. You can prefer not to answer any of them.

wpt.label: More independent access for some users

v2g.label: An active role in managing stored energy

wpt: Possible value depends on your situation and the installation. Consider these possibilities:
With a compatible vehicle and correctly placed pad, wireless charging can avoid manually connecting a cable.
A suitable installation can fit a planned parking stay. Cable charging can also do this; this is not a wireless speed advantage.
Authorised positioning assistance may help place the vehicle correctly, with supervision and stop controls.
Avoiding cable handling may support independent use if layout, controls and support suit the person’s needs.
v2g: Possible value depends on your situation, the contract and how the service operates. Consider these possibilities:
A household may receive compensation under agreed availability conditions, potentially below the maximum; energy reimbursement is separate.
Agreed battery export may help match electricity supply and demand, depending on service and grid conditions.
Coordinated charging/export may support variable renewable generation. The effect depends on timing, supply and operation.
Households may contribute stored energy under their reserve, schedule and permissions while retaining stop and withdrawal controls.
